payload.title: Claim about a dropped ball and a horizontally launched ball

stimulus.description: Two identical small balls are at the edge of a horizontal platform of height $h=1.8\text{ m}$. At the same instant one ball is dropped from rest and the other is launched horizontally with speed $v_0=3\text{ m/s}$. Air resistance is negligible. A student claims that the ball that is launched horizontally takes longer to reach the floor because it travels farther.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Do you agree or disagree with the student's claim? Justify your answer qualitatively without calculating numbers.
parts.model_answer: Disagree. The horizontal and vertical motions are independent. Both balls start with zero vertical velocity and have the same vertical acceleration $g$ over the same height, so they reach the floor at the same time.

rubric_rows.criterion: Disagrees with the claim (the two balls land at the same time)
common_errors: agrees because the launched ball travels a longer path

rubric_rows.criterion: Justifies that the vertical motion does not depend on the horizontal motion
required_elements: vertical and horizontal motions are independent
common_errors: argues only that gravity acts on both balls

rubric_rows.criterion: Notes that both balls have the same initial vertical velocity (zero), the same acceleration and the same height
required_elements: same initial vertical velocity, acceleration and height
common_errors: states the launched ball has a larger vertical acceleration

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the time that the balls take to reach the floor in terms of $h$ and fundamental constants, and calculate the horizontal distance from the platform edge at which the launched ball lands.
parts.model_answer: $h=\tfrac12gt^2$ so $t=\sqrt{2h/g}=0.606\text{ s}$; the horizontal distance is $x=v_0t=1.82\text{ m}$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Applies the vertical kinematic equation $h=\tfrac12gt^2$ with zero initial vertical velocity
common_errors: uses $h=v_0t$

rubric_rows.criterion: Solves for the time $t=\sqrt{2h/g}$
common_errors: omits the square root

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates a landing distance of about 1.82 with units of meters using $x=v_0t$
common_errors: uses the total speed in the horizontal distance

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: The launch speed of the horizontal ball is doubled to $6\text{ m/s}$ while the platform height stays the same. Predict how the time to reach the floor and the landing distance change, and justify your prediction.
parts.model_answer: The time stays the same because it depends only on the height, and the landing distance doubles because $x=v_0t$ with the same time.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that the time stays the same and the landing distance doubles
common_errors: states that the time halves

rubric_rows.criterion: Justifies with $t=\sqrt{2h/g}$ independent of $v_0$ and $x=v_0t$ proportional to $v_0$
required_elements: t independent of v0 and x proportional to v0
common_errors: argues that a faster ball spends less time in the air
